purpose: Compose synthetic read-only ffprobe-style metadata with an editorial sidecar using identity hash and source version without adding a new media core.

activities.label: join ffprobe-style metadata and editorial sidecar by asset identity hash and source version
attack stale sidecars conflicting identities ranges markers synchronization provenance and write permissions
record the shortcut result and remaining live-media unknowns

queries.expression: can ffprobe-style metadata be completed by a sidecar without losing asset identity hash and version provenance
are source ranges marker position and audio video sync preserved with exact rational time
do stale identity range marker sync provenance and write violations block composition
does the shortcut reuse the shared CloudEvents replay and read-only kernel without installing media infrastructure

assumptions: Both ffprobe-style metadata and the editorial sidecar are synthetic payloads modeled after documented concepts, not live tool output.
The source version and content hash are authoritative only within the declared synthetic source registry.
A sidecar completes only the missing editorial semantics; it cannot grant rights or playback capability.
Read-only normalization and dry-run composition do not imply export or execution permission.
Exact rational values are required for timebase ranges marker mapping and synchronization.
kill_tests: A stale sidecar hash blocks composition.
A stale sidecar source version blocks composition.
A sidecar for another asset blocks composition.
A source range outside the asset available range blocks composition.
A marker source frame inconsistent with the source record blocks composition.
Missing sidecar provenance references block composition.
A writable sidecar policy blocks the adapter.
A non-dry-run action blocks the adapter.
A missing required input event blocks the shared envelope.
unknowns: Whether a real sidecar needs signatures or an external authority beyond ref hash and version.
Whether file replacement and concurrent sidecars require a conflict/version vector contract.
Whether VFR drop-frame keyframes transitions effects and time-warp need a media contract extension.
Whether rights and player capability can be independently verified in a live system.
Whether a real ffprobe adapter preserves the same fields and failure modes as this fixture.
